newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC Corp falls on ratings downgrade.
newsitem.headline: NEC Corp falls on ratings downgrade.

text.p: NEC Corp shares fell in the afternoon trading session on Monday after a major brokerage revised the company's ratings downward, brokers said.
As of 0450 GMT, the shares were down 60 yen at 1,600.
It was the second most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse with volume totalling 3.71 million shares.
Nomura Securities Co Ltd downgraded NEC to a "2" rating from its previous "1", market sources said on Monday.

In its three-grade rating system, Nomura assigns a 2 rating to issues whose values it sees moving within 10 percentage points in either direction of the key 225-share Nikkei average over the next six months.
According to Nomura Securities, NEC's investment in Packard Bell NEC (PB-NEC) was accumulating and there was a risk that the firm might not be able to recover its investment.
NEC said on Monday it would invest an additional $285 million in PB-NEC to help the U.S. firm strengthen its business in office-use personal computers.
Nomura also said the effect of a fall in DRAM prices on NEC's earnings could not be ignored.
